description: Policy for the AI RMF questionnaire at engagement time. build_ai_questions.py picks a client's questions from the two banks (data/ai/banks/question_bank_ai_rmf_<foundation|areas>.json) by filtering on the usage profile (runs/<Org>_<date>/ai_usage.json): the roles the client is asked as (client_roles), its producer flags and, for area questions, its AI areas. Change policy by editing this file, not the code.

ai_area_rules.description: Which AI areas (data/ai/ai_areas.json) a client gets, besides the ones ticked in the intake menus ai_usage and ai_components: always, any_ai (AI in use), role (the answer to "Do you build AI, use AI, or both?") and with (an area that brings others). Every AI area must be reachable (a test checks it).

client_roles.description: The question roles a client is asked as, by AI in use (none, unsure) or, when AI is in use, by the answer to "Do you build AI, use AI, or both?". A question is picked when one of its roles is here. Unsure is asked as a consumer, plus the questions for an org with no AI (AI policy, shadow AI).

usage_notes.none: No AI use declared: only the AI policy and shadow-AI questions are asked
usage_notes.unsure: AI use unconfirmed: asked as a consumer; discover what AI is in use before assuming any

engagement_flags.description: The engagement flags ai_usage.json must carry (intake.py). They do not change which AI questions are asked or how: every AI question is about AI (an AI area, or AI in the organisation), so it never repeats the general security the CSF sheet or ISO 27001 covers, and is full_discovery for every client. The client may cite a general control as evidence; the assessor checks whether it reaches the AI.

review_flag: LOW — bank entry flagged for human review; assessor verification required
